title: align emission windows to kernel batch boundaries and add KV compaction prefetch
author: Evelyn Chen
release_notes: Align emission windows with kernel batch boundaries to reduce first-byte latency; introduce lightweight KV cache compaction and prefetch hints for long-lived streams; no API changes.
description:
Summary: Reduce streaming first-byte latency by aligning per-stream emission windows to kernel batch boundaries, adding a compact KV-prefetch path for stalled streams, and introducing a light-weight handoff to next microbatch when kernels are warm.

Motivation: we observed recurring small delays at stream boundaries where the emitter would flush a tiny payload that did not match the GPU kernel batch size; that triggered kernel invocation overhead and inefficient CUDA launches for micro-batches. For long-lived conversations, cold KV pages and scatter prefetches also introduced tail spikes.

Goals: 1) shape emission timing so emitted tokens more often land inside a kernel-sized bundle; 2) avoid kernel invocation for sub-threshold emissions by deferring via a short, adaptive hold window; 3) provide a compact KV compaction/prefetch path that warms only actively referenced KV shards without full rehydrate; 4) keep changes opt-in via a scheduler flag and a conservative default.

Design:
- Emission window alignment: emitter calculates a per-stream phase based on recent sequence lengths and kernel target_batch_size. Instead of flushing immediately on token availability, emitter waits up to align_window_ms (default 4ms, configurable) to try and batch into an already-scheduled kernel slot. The window is bounded and won't exceed configured latency SLOs.
- Kernel boundary hints: runtime now exposes lightweight kernel_batch_boundary() hints that the scheduler can use to group streams with similar phase into the same kernel invocation.
- Adaptive hold policy: a soft hold with exponential backoff for cold streams; holds are preemptible by latency-critical streams and honor stream deadlines.
- KV compaction prefetch: introduces kv_compact_prefetch mode which maintains a compact working set summary per stream and issues narrow prefetches for only hot KV ranges on handoff; this avoids rehydrating large KV pages for small shifts in attention.
- Microbatch handoff API: small change to the executor internals to support preemptive microbatch handoff when a kernel reports "hot" caches and the queued streams are aligned.

All changes gated behind feature flag: runtime.optim.emit_align_v1 and runtime.kv.compact_prefetch.

Commits (high-level):
- 7 commits: initial design + phase calculator, scheduler hook, kernel hint plumbing, KV compact prefetch implementation, unit tests, perf harness + benchmark results, docs for flags.

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/emitter/phase_calculator.rs: new logic for per-stream phase and window timers
- runtime/scheduler/batch_planner.rs: uses kernel boundary hints to form kernel groups
- runtime/kernel/metadata.rs: adds boundary hint API
- runtime/kv/compact_prefetch.rs: new compact prefetch implementation and small LRU summaries
- runtime/executor/microbatch_handoff.rs: handoff path and low-overhead signaling
- tests/unit/emit_align_tests.rs
- docs/flags/emit_align.md (docs + quick tuning guide)

Benchmarks:
- Local perf-harness run on p3dn (48GB) using chat-bench scenario (avg prompt length 80 tokens, mean response 32 tokens)
- Results: median TTFB down 18% (from 28ms→23ms), P95 TTFB down 33% (from 94ms→63ms) on mixed workload; small throughput regression (<2%) at very high concurrency due to slightly increased batching wait; KV compaction reduced cold-stream tail spikes by ~45% in targeted long-conversation tests.

Backwards compatibility: no API changes. Feature gated and off by default for safety in production.

Rollout plan:
1) land behind flags, internal canary on dedicated infra
2) enable compact_prefetch on low-traffic regions
3) widen kernel-alignment flag after 2 weeks of monitoring.

Reviewer notes & discussion (excerpted, chronological):
- Marco: "Nice approach. Please document how this interacts with existing prefix caching and the KV evictor."
- Author: "Added section in docs/flags explaining interaction: compact_prefetch only reads summary-based ranges and will not evict; full rehydrate still happens for full-checkpoint restores."
- Priya: "Concern: how do we avoid a pathological case where all streams align and create enormous kernels?"
- Author: "We cap group sizes by kernel_target_size and introduce fair scheduling heuristics; added unit test to simulate alignment storms."
- Noah: "Can we get an opt-in metric for held-milliseconds per stream for SLO monitoring?"
- Author: "Added metric runtime.emit_align.hold_ms and a console dashboard note in the docs."

CI and validation:
- CI flaky on first run: lint failure fixed (trailing whitespace)
- Unit tests: all green locally and in CI after fix
- Perf harness: included microbench scripts under tools/perf/emit_align/
- CI summary: build — pass, unit-tests — pass, bench-smoke — pass, lint — pass (after 1st fix), e2e on small dedicated cluster — pass.

Merge notes:
- After reviewers approved, squashed and merged via "squash-merge" to main.
- Deploy toggles added to internal rollout script.

Related work and references:
- Related PRs on kernel grouping in the past: see ENG-2859 design notes and follow-on ENG-3412 (kernel affinity improvements).
- This PR's linear tickets: ENG-3621 (emit window feature), ENG-3679 (kv compact prefetch).

Caveats and limitations:
- Works best when median response tokens per turn > 6; for extreme sub-token responses benefit is limited.
- Small increased batching wait may slightly increase tail throughput in the highest concurrency regimes; tuned defaults optimize for latency SLOs, not raw throughput.
